payload.task_text:
The e-commerce manager wants a monthly sales performance presentation to share with stakeholders and needs a planning meeting scheduled. Analyze WooCommerce order data broken down by month to compute monthly revenue totals and order counts across all order statuses.

Create a PowerPoint presentation called Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx with the following slides. Slide 1 should be a title slide with "Monthly Sales Performance Review" as the title. Slide 2 should be titled "Monthly Revenue Overview" and contain a table showing each month (January through December), the number of orders, and the total revenue for that month. Slide 3 should be titled "Order Volume Trends" and describe the monthly order volume patterns. Slide 4 should be titled "Key Insights" and highlight the peak revenue month, the lowest revenue month, and total annual revenue. Slide 5 should be titled "Next Steps" with planned actions for improving sales performance.

Schedule a Google Calendar event called "Monthly Sales Review" on 2026-04-15 from 14:00 to 15:00 with a description noting it is a stakeholder review of monthly sales performance.

Email the presentation to ecommerce_manager@store.com with subject "Monthly Sales Performance Review" and include the key revenue highlights in the email body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. The complete order catalog, twelve monthly rows, five-slide deck, one fixed meeting, and one email form one compact workflow.

Resolve the workspace dynamically. Start the independent meeting inventory and order retrieval in the same response: call `list_events(timeMin="2026-04-15T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-04-16T00:00:00", maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime")`, and call `woo_orders_list(perPage=100,page=1)` without `status`. Continue increasing order pages until a short or empty page, preserving all observed statuses; do not query by status/month and do not modify orders. Parse every observed order date and numeric total once, aggregate January through December counts and revenue including zero months, and freeze peak month, lowest month, and annual revenue with deterministic source-order tie handling.

Create `Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx` exactly once with one presentation ID and exactly the five requested slides, including all twelve monthly rows and insights derived only from the frozen table; read back the full slide inventory and verify every title/value. Filter the event inventory locally to exact `Monthly Sales Review` at 14:00–15:00, create once only if missing with exact `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime` and description, retain the created/reused ID, and call `get_event`. Only after deck and event readback, check Sent mail for the exact recipient/subject; send one missing email with verified highlights and the presentation in the supported workspace-path `attachments` list, never retry an ambiguous send, and read back the attachment record before `claim_done`.

nodes.text:
You are analyzing a WooCommerce store's order data for a monthly sales review. I need monthly aggregates across ALL order statuses (read-only task — do not modify anything).

Method:
1. Use mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list. Fetch ALL orders: paginate with perPage=100, page=1,2,3,... until a page returns fewer than 100 items. Do NOT filter by date. First try without a status filter; if the API defaults to a subset of statuses, also fetch each remaining status explicitly (pending, processing, on-hold, completed, cancelled, refunded, failed) and merge.
2. For each order capture: "date_created" and "total".
3. Group by calendar month of date_created (January–December).

Report back (self-contained, since downstream steps rely only on your output):
- Which year(s) appear in the data and how many orders per year.
- A table with columns: Month (January..December) | Number of Orders | Total Revenue (sum of order totals, $ formatted, 2 decimals) for ALL twelve months (use 0 / $0.00 for months with no orders).
- Peak revenue month and its revenue.
- Lowest revenue month that has orders (if a month has zero orders, note it but treat the lowest month-with-orders as lowest for reporting) and its revenue.
- Total annual revenue (sum across all months) and total number of orders.
- Month with the highest order count (peak volume month) and its count, plus the average monthly order count (1 decimal).

Format revenue values with $ and 2 decimals (e.g., $12,345.67). Return the exact numbers; they will be pasted into a presentation.
Aggregate WooCommerce orders monthly

Build a PowerPoint presentation and save it to exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-wc-order-monthly-ppt-gcal/workspace/Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx

The deck is a monthly sales performance review for an e-commerce store (WooCommerce data, USD). It must contain exactly 5 slides with the content below. Use the pptx MCP tools (e.g., create_presentation / create_presentation_from_templates or add_slide + add_table + manage_text). After saving, verify the file exists at the exact path and extract/re-check text to confirm all 5 slide titles and the table numbers are present. Use a clean, professional business style (e.g., modern_blue scheme).

SLIDE 1 — Title slide:
- Title: "Monthly Sales Performance Review"
- Subtitle (optional, short): "Monthly Order & Revenue Analysis — WooCommerce Store Data"

SLIDE 2 — Title: "Monthly Revenue Overview"
- Content: a table with 13 rows (header + 12 months) and 3 columns: Month | Orders | Total Revenue. Use exactly these values:
  January, 14, $5,938.09
  February, 13, $5,615.02
  March, 14, $2,089.69
  April, 9, $4,349.71
  May, 10, $6,023.29
  June, 11, $9,555.69
  July, 8, $3,921.19
  August, 17, $3,873.37
  September, 17, $5,842.43
  October, 11, $4,447.76
  November, 9, $1,212.05
  December, 17, $8,843.75
- Make the table fit the slide (moderate font size, e.g., header 12pt, body 10pt); size it so all 13 rows are visible.

SLIDE 3 — Title: "Order Volume Trends"
- Bullet points describing the monthly order-volume pattern (use these facts, wording can be concise):
  * 150 orders across the year — an average of 12.5 orders per month
  * Peak order volume: August, September and December tied at 17 orders each
  * Slowest months by volume: July (8 orders), April and November (9 orders each)
  * Volume is strongest in late Q3 and Q4, but high volume does not always mean high revenue (e.g., August had 17 orders yet only $3,873.37 in revenue)
  * Steady baseline demand: every month recorded at least 8 orders

SLIDE 4 — Title: "Key Insights"
- Bullet points:
  * Peak revenue month: June — $9,555.69 (11 orders)
  * Lowest revenue month: November — $1,212.05 (9 orders)
  * Total annual revenue: $61,712.04 across 150 orders
  * Runners-up: December ($8,843.75) and may ($6,023.29) — note: write "May ($6,023.29)" correctly
  * Revenue per order varies widely by month, signalling inconsistent average order value

SLIDE 5 — Title: "Next Steps"
- Bullet points with planned actions:
  * Launch targeted promotions in low-revenue months (November, March, July) to lift sales
  * Replicate June and December campaign tactics that drove peak revenue
  * Improve average order value in high-volume, low-revenue months (e.g., August) via bundling and upsells
  * Prepare inventory, staffing and marketing ahead of the August–December high-volume period
  * Establish a monthly KPI review to track revenue, order counts and trends

Deliverable/acceptance: the .pptx file saved at the exact path above, containing exactly these 5 slides with the specified titles, the full 12-month table with exact numbers, and the bullets. Report back the final file path and a confirmation of what you verified (slide titles + table spot checks).
Build Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx
